<!-- pr-reviewer: f9904306767348db491d83a5e4d016c881577415 -->
<!-- review-cost: effort:high · escalated: no -->
Reviewed head f99043067. The trial merge with main is clean.

The refusal law holds. One door decides the aligned setup:
`collect_job` calls `setup_align::generation_problem`
(crates/app/src/operation/job.rs:177). The kind list and the refusal
message changed together (crates/app/src/setup_align.rs:375, 398).
No other copy of the list exists in the code, the UI or the docs.
The align page stores a transform only; it has no per-kind branch.

The accepted path applies the setup transform. The chamfer reads the
material through `setup_align::facets_in`
(crates/app/src/operation/material.rs:231), the area through the
section of those facets (crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs:209),
the top plane through `part_aabb_in`
(crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs:68), and the picks through
`pose_in_setup` (crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs:293). These
are the same doors as 2D Contour. The proof test pins both sides:
the turned setup and the baked part post one program; the part as
modelled cuts another path
(crates/app/tests/setup_align_chamfer.rs:181, 225). The lathe
Chamfering kind stays refused in an aligned setup, by name.

Gate on the merged tree: setup_align_chamfer 2 pass; opframe_picks 4
pass; setup_align 10 pass; setup_align_2d_kinds 8 pass; camcraft-app
lib 360 pass, 1 ignored; clippy -D warnings clean.

Note (no action): only the picked-edge source is proved in a turned
setup. The whole-model source takes the same setup-frame doors
(material_source.rs:209), so it is wired, but no test covers it in
that frame. A small follow-up would cover it.

Verdict: clean. Proposed label: merge-ready.
